_comment: Single source of truth for the relay rules, shared by relay.mjs and every agent session. 'allowed' is the AUTHORITATIVE permission list: an edge is permitted iff it is listed here. 'chain' documents the linear pipeline order (the chain agents have only neighbour edges in 'allowed', so their adjacency is enforced implicitly). The owner<->interpreter edge is exercised in the Interpreter's live session with the human, not via mailbox, but is recorded here so its messages still validate when written to the ledger. The SENTINEL stands outside the chain and, via the sentinel>* edges below, may speak one-way to ANY agent (advisory/warning/directive) to keep communication on-contract; no agent replies to it. The QA reviewer also stands outside the chain: via the qa>builder edge it sends one-way test-design reviews (Farley Index quality of the Builder's tests) to the Builder, who does not reply. The WARDEN (security expert) likewise stands outside the chain: via the warden>builder edge it sends one-way security reviews (vulnerabilities and violations of common security patterns in the Builder's code) to the Builder, who does not reply. The REAPER (mutation testing) likewise stands outside the chain: via the reaper>builder edge it sends one-way mutation-testing results (surviving mutants = gaps in the Builder's tests) to the Builder, who does not reply — this is deliberately pulled out of the Builder's own loop because mutation testing is slow, and runs out-of-band after commits land instead of blocking the Builder's TDD cycle. The COURIER (acceptance-test runner) likewise stands outside the chain: via the courier>builder edge it sends one-way acceptance-suite results (which BDD scenarios pass/fail across the whole accumulated suite) to the Builder, who does not reply — re-running the whole suite inline got slower as it grew, so it was pulled out to run out-of-band on a fast cadence, trading a bit of risk (a regression is caught after the fact, not before the next commit) for the Builder never blocking on it. A 'broadcast' is an EXTRAORDINARY message the Owner can send to pass an instruction down the WHOLE line: it is allowed on every downward edge (owner>interpreter>analyst>examiner>builder) and each agent applies it then forwards it on, unchanged in intent, to its downstream neighbour.
